why: A taste test of a ready meal with 8,000 customers and 15,000 non-customers is believable, and every rating distribution adds to 100%.
An ice-cream parlour taking about $42,000 a month from roughly 12,400 servings (about $3.40 each) is believable, and the margins match revenue minus costs.

A small motoring club with 54k members making 92,000 call-outs at £4.1m fixed plus £100 a call-out is believable; the group member counts add to 54k and cost per head falls from Group A to Group E as stated.
A capital-city bus operator with about 31 million journeys and $53 million revenue a month is believable, profit equals revenue minus costs, and the average month lengths are correct.
Online and showroom profits add to the stated totals, and the margins imply steady sales of about $0.8-1 billion, believable for a furniture retailer with loss-making showrooms.
Export market shares of 0.6% to 6.2% and margins of 11% to 24% fit a kitchen equipment maker with a modest presence abroad.
Bread consumption of about 57 to 71 kg per person a year, loaf prices of $0.90 to $2.00 and costs below price are all believable.

The chart says countries run from biggest to smallest, yet country 10 adds 2.7 points after country 9 adds 1.5, and country 35 adds 1.5 points after country 34 adds 0, so the running total cannot be ordered as stated.
1.5 million candles of 0.3 kg each from two factories, with wax at $2 to $5 per kg and a volume price break, is believable.
About 1,500 to 1,800 agents paid $15 to $17 an hour, answering around 11 to 13 calls per paid hour on calls, is believable for a helpline outsourcer.
